# Full source cores do not keep radial centers uniformly inside the envelope

This is an exact diagnostic for the proposed discrete Ball-body route. It
retains a full-dimensional occupied homothetic source core with an interior
integer point and a global positive affine envelope. It disproves choosing
the centroid of that envelope as the radial center, and any uniform
interiority conclusion for successful centers. It does NOT disprove the
existence of an uncentered convex subbody of volume M/2^n in each radial
body, or the existence of a suitable movable centered subbody. Actual H
criticality of the designated sources is not claimed.

## 1. A compatible family in every integer dimension

Fix n>=2,d>=1,N>=4. Put D=[-1,1]^d, V=2^d, v=e_1, and write the base
as z=(j,k) with

    -1<=j<=N,   k in [-1,1]^(n-1).

Use ell(z)=j+2, y(z)=0, and fibers independent of k:

    K_j=(j+2)D                  for -1<=j<=1,
    K_j=3D+(j-1)v               for 1<=j<=N.              (1)

These are the exact fibers of a convex body. Indeed their support
functions are

    h_j(u)=min{(j+2)h_D(u), 3h_D(u)+(j-1)u.v},

where the first affine branch is selected before j=1 and the second
afterwards, since u.v<=h_D(u). Thus h_j(u) is concave in j for every u,
which proves every required Minkowski interpolation inclusion. Equivalently
the body is the convex hull of the fibers at j=-1,1,N, times the remaining
base box.

The complete integer support is the entire corresponding integer box;
all fibers have positive d-volume. Also

    K_z subset ell(z)D

because, for j>=1, 3D+(j-1)v is contained in (j+2)D by v in D. Equality
holds throughout the full-dimensional source box B=[-1,1]^n, whose
interior contains the integer point0. Thus there is no hollow-core or
missing-integer issue in this example.

Let A=3^(n-1). The original mixed mass is exactly

    M=A V [1+2^d+N 3^d].                                 (2)

## 2. Exact pointed density and a bounded negative cap

The pointed density of the actual family is

    f_N(xi)=A[(1+2^d+3^d)1_D(xi)
              +sum_(j=2)^N (j+2)^d 1_(D_j)(xi)],
    D_j=3D/(j+2)+(j-1)v/(j+2)
       =v+[3/(j+2)](D-v).                                (3)

Its integral is M. Notice that the outside pointed fibers shrink toward
the actual boundary point v; their weights exactly retain physical mass.

At the source-envelope centroid c=0, the cap xi_1<=0 has exact mass

    Q_0=A V [(1+2^d)/2+3^d].                             (4)

To check it without any projective measure substitution, in physical
fiber j the cap is X_1<=0. Fibers j=-1,0 contribute half their volumes.
Among the constant-volume fibers, j=1,2,3 contribute the fractions
1/2,1/3,1/6, whose sum is1; j>=4 contribute zero d-volume.

Define the Ball radial set at c by

    rho_c(u)^d=d integral_0^infinity t^(d-1) f_N(c+t u)dt.

Polar coordinates give |R_c|=M and preserve every halfspace through c:

    |R_c intersect {u.w<=0}|=integral_(u.(xi-c)<=0) f_N.
                                                               (5)

Consequently any convex body L contained in R_0 whose centroid is0 obeys,
by ordinary Gruenbaum,

    |L| <= Q_0/Gamma_d.                                  (6)

It therefore cannot have volume M/2^n whenever

    1+2^d+N3^d > (2^n/Gamma_d)[(1+2^d)/2+3^d].           (7)

For the entirely rational small choice n=d=2,N=11, the values are

    M=1248, Q_0=138, Gamma_2 M/4=416/3>138,
    |L|<=621/2=310.5 < M/4=312.

Thus a radial proof must actually move its center; centering at the
source body's ordinary centroid fails even with this genuine full-rank
source geometry. This is not a contradiction to a theorem allowing the
center to move toward v.

## 3. Every successful center approaches the boundary at a quantified rate

Let c in D, eta=1-c_1>0. In physical fiber j>=1 the cap xi_1<=c_1 becomes

    X_1<=(j+2)c_1.

Its threshold lies below the entire fiber as soon as

    (j+2)(1-c_1)>=6.

Hence, using only whole-fiber upper bounds,

    integral_(xi_1<=c_1) f_N
       <=A V [1+2^d+(6/eta)3^d].                         (8)

If some centroid-zero convex L contained in R_c has |L|>=M/2^n, (5)
and ordinary Gruenbaum require this cap mass to be at least
Gamma_d M/2^n. Whenever the denominator below is positive, therefore

    1-c_1 <= 6 3^d /
      [(Gamma_d/2^n)(1+2^d+N3^d)-(1+2^d)].              (9)

In particular c_1 approaches1 at rate O(1/N). For each l>=2, use the
cap xi_l>=c_l if c_l>0 and xi_l<=c_l if c_l<0. It misses every outside
fiber with j+2>3/|c_l|. The same argument gives

    |c_l| <= 3 3^d /
      [(Gamma_d/2^n)(1+2^d+N3^d)-(1+2^d)].              (10)

Thus every such successful center tends to v, not just to an unspecified
boundary face. More generally (9)--(10) hold with any asserted normalized
ordinary pointed depth delta in place of Gamma_d/2^n.

This also applies to ACTUAL ordinary deepest points of f_N: their depth
is at least M/(d+1), by the ordinary centerpoint theorem for absolutely
continuous finite measures, so replace Gamma_d/2^n by 1/(d+1). All those
maximizers therefore tend to v at rate O(1/N). No claim of actual mixed
maximality at the designated source bases is used or needed.

## 4. Exact cancellation of pointed weights in the radial integral

For any affine source chart y(z),ell(z)>0 and ANY c, the pointed radial
integral has the elementary identity

    ell_z^d d integral_0^infinity t^(d-1)
           1_(K_z)(y_z+ell_z c+ell_z t u)dt
      =d integral_0^infinity s^(d-1)
           1_(K_z-y_z-ell_z c)(s u)ds.                   (11)

The substitution is s=ell_z t. Thus pointed radial sets are exactly the
radial sets of the ORIGINAL uniform fiber measures after the single
actual affine shear X -> X-y(z)-ell(z)c. No transformed lattice and no
weighted replacement law is hidden in (11).

The unresolved target remains a convex-subbody capacity theorem with a
valid movable-centroid selection. Equations (6)--(10) rule out fixing the
center at the source centroid or invoking uniform interior compactness
for that selection. They do not rule out the target itself.
